The closest matches are [1], [2], [3], and [8]. [1] directly focuses on predicting short-term item popularity with a fine-tuned LLM and generating explanations, while [2] and [3] use LLMs to improve recommendation ranking and explainability through re-ranking or selective guidance. [8] addresses popularity bias in recommendation with LLM-based semantic understanding, but it is about debiasing rather than popularity prediction itself.

None of these papers is a pure “LLM popularity prediction recommendation” paper in the general sense, but [1] is the most directly aligned if you mean predicting item popularity for recommendation. [2], [3], and [8] are related alternatives that use LLMs to improve recommendation quality, interpretability, or fairness rather than primarily forecasting popularity.
